newsitem.title: POLAND: Swedish PM in Poland to help after floods.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM in Poland to help after floods.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson on Thursday visited Poland's southwestern regions, devastated by July's flooding, to determine how his country could help in their reconstruction.

"Sweden's prime minister is on a working visit to learn about the flood situation on the spot and see what help could be extended by Sweden," Polish Foreign Ministry spokesman Przemyslaw Antoniewicz said.
Persson, who arrived in the southwestern city of Wroclaw, was scheduled to fly in a helicopter to flood-hit provinces of Walbrzych and Opole to inspect the scope of damage, PAP news agency reported.
Persson was accompanied by Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz during his one-day visit, PAP said.

The floods, which hit Poland a month ago, killing 54 people and swamping more than 6,600 sq km (2,500 sq miles), caused damage running into billions of dollars by demolishing buildings, roads, railways and bridges, and by destroying crops.
Nearly 1,700 sq km (660 sq miles) were still under water on Thursday and over 30,000 people remained displaced, but the floodwaters were receding.
The River Oder on the border with Germany subsided and the mayor of the town of Slubice, which had been threatened by flooding, asked its evacuated residents to return home.
